title: DNS over QUIC RFC 9250 Stream Lifecycle Architecture
purpose: Define the minimal DoQ query/response stream lifecycle above the managed QUIC transport.
design_summary: The DoQ stream lifecycle is implemented in `Incursa.Quic.Dns` as an adapter over `QuicConnection` and `QuicStream`. `DoqClient` opens a new client-initiated bidirectional stream for every query, sets the DNS Message ID field to zero, writes one length-prefixed DNS message, completes writes to send STREAM FIN, reads one response from the same stream, and then disposes the stream. `DoqServer` accepts QUIC connections from a listener, accepts inbound bidirectional streams, and handles each query stream independently through `IDoqQueryHandler`, writing the response on the same stream and completing writes after the response bytes.
data_and_state_considerations: The stream lifecycle uses the foundation `DoqMessageCodec` for message boundaries and relies on QUIC stream IDs for transaction correlation. The adapter does not require DNS Message ID correlation for DoQ-local request/response matching. Server stream handlers are scheduled independently so multiple queries can be in flight on one persistent connection.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Only bidirectional streams are accepted for DoQ query/response transactions in this slice.
The server may wait until the complete length-prefixed query is available before dispatching to the handler.
Incomplete DoQ frames fail deterministically with `DOQ_PROTOCOL_ERROR` through `DoqException`.
Gateway-specific DNS Message ID generation when forwarding from DoQ to another transport remains outside this slice.
risks: This slice proves minimal one-response transactions only; AXFR/IXFR multi-response behavior needs a later stream sequencing design.
Cancellation, STOP_SENDING, RESET_STREAM, dangling stream limits, and excessive load policy need separate proof because they affect error handling and resource limits.
External DoQ interop should wait until cancellation, padding, and lifecycle policies are trace-owned.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: The DoQ adapter owns query/response stream mapping. The QUIC transport remains responsible for opening, accepting, reading, writing, FIN, flow control, and TLS. DNS resolver behavior remains behind `IDoqQueryHandler`.
